definitions.explanation: lasting only a short time; easily lost or destroyed; having a fragile, impermanent quality

examples.japanese: ⟦{人生|じんせい}→人生：03355_jinsei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{儚|はかな}い。
⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{美|うつく}しさ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{儚|はかな}い⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦こそ→こそ：12731_koso⟧⟦{愛|あい}される→愛する：01811_aisuru⟧。
examples.english: Cherry blossoms are loved precisely because their beauty is fleeting.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{儚|はかな}い⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{印象|いんしょう}→印象：01846_inshou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: Her fragile smile left an impression on me.

notes:
{儚|はかな}い expresses the transient, ephemeral nature of things, often with a sense of beauty or sadness.

FORMS:
- Attributive: {儚|はかな}い + noun
- Predicate: {儚|はかな}い
- Adverbial: {儚|はかな}く
- Noun form: {儚|はかな}さ (transience)

WRITING:
- The kanji {儚|はかな} ({人|にんべん} + ⟦{夢|ゆめ}→夢：01519_yume⟧) literally suggests "person + dream," evoking the dreamlike, insubstantial quality of fleeting things.
- Often written in hiragana (はかない) in modern usage.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Central to Japanese aesthetics (⟦{物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ→物の哀れ：30312_mononoaware⟧)
- Associated with cherry blossoms, fireflies, and other symbols of transience
- Reflects Buddhist concepts of impermanence (⟦{無常|むじょう}→無常：13422_mujou⟧)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {儚|はかな}い⟦{命|いのち}→命：02371_inochi⟧ (fleeting life)
- {儚|はかな}い⟦{夢|ゆめ}→夢：01519_yume⟧ (ephemeral dream)
- {儚|はかな}い{美|うつく}しさ (transient beauty)
- {儚|はかな}い⟦{希望|きぼう}→希望：00221_kibou⟧ (fragile hope)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{短|みじか}い→短い：00510_mijikai⟧ (short - neutral, objective)
- ⟦{束|つか}の{間|ま}→束の間：12863_tsukanoma⟧ (momentary - time-focused)
- ⟦{脆|もろ}い→脆い：06069_moroi⟧ (fragile - physical fragility)

REGISTER: Literary/formal. Often used in poetry and emotional contexts.
